guard: The fixed-group npm census refuses partial, incomplete, or stage-only releases before any registry write
why: A sequential recursive publish cannot recover after one package version lands and a later package refuses.
npm OIDC HTTP 201 proves identity, not the direct-publish Allowed action. These mutations remove one fail-before-write property at a time and every one must be killed by the fake registry smoke.

mutations.name: a census state literal is renamed in the published union
mutations.note: Graded separately from preflightNpmPublish because the two properties are emitted independently: before this fix each was its own bare `string`, so one entry point's coverage says nothing about the other's. This mutation widens the declared return rather than deleting it, and the difference was measured: DELETING the annotation here does not widen anything, because this function returns preflightNpmPublish(...) directly and inherits the union by inference, so a deletion reds the byte-identity cell instead and grades WRONG-RED. The annotation is kept in the source anyway, because inference only holds while the body stays a direct return.

mutations.name: a bare return is added to readExactVersion, yielding undefined, which no census bucket claims
mutations.expectRed: return statements the compiler finds in readExactVersion each yield present, absent or an unknown: value
mutations.cell: return statements the compiler finds in readExactVersion each yield present, absent or an unknown: value
mutations.note: The escape that killed the retired regex extractor: /\breturn\s+([^;]+);/ requires a non-empty expression, so a bare return was invisible to it and the universal cell stayed green while the function gained an undefined return.

mutations.name: a semicolon-free out-of-domain return is added, closed by ASI

mutations.note: The retired regex captured to the next semicolon, so a semicolon-free return was swallowed into the following return's text and laundered into the domain.

mutations.name: the shipped absent bucket is widened to also claim unknown rows, so a row lands in two buckets
mutations.expectRed: under the shipped bucket predicates every production census row lands in exactly one bucket
mutations.cell: under the shipped bucket predicates every production census row lands in exactly one bucket
mutations.note: The overlap the previous disjointness cell documented but could not detect: it retyped the predicates, so widening the SHIPPED one left the copy green. This cell imports the shipped predicate, so the widening changes what it computes.

mutations.name: the return enumerator stops treating a bare return as out of domain
mutations.find: if (!expression) return { text, inDomain: false, why: "bare return: yields undefined, which no census bucket claims" };
mutations.replace: if (!expression) return { text, inDomain: true, why: "bare return: yields undefined, which no census bucket claims" };
mutations.expectRed: the return enumerator refuses a bare return, which yields undefined
mutations.cell: the return enumerator refuses a bare return, which yields undefined
mutations.note: Grades the instrument rather than the subject: if the enumerator stops refusing a bare return, the escape cell that pins that refusal must red. Without this the enumerator could be silently relaxed back to the defect it replaced.

mutations.name: the return enumerator descends into nested functions, attributing their returns to readExactVersion
mutations.expectRed: a return inside a nested function is not attributed to readExactVersion
mutations.cell: a return inside a nested function is not attributed to readExactVersion
mutations.note: The false-positive half of the enumerator: a helper closure's return is not readExactVersion's. Without the boundary the enumerator would red the shipped source for a value the function never returns.

mutations.name: a CENSUS_BUCKETS entry drifts off the exported predicate onto an equivalent inline copy

mutations.cell: each CENSUS_BUCKETS entry is the exported predicate object itself
mutations.note: Found by attacking the bucket cells: the table this suite grades through agreed with the ladder today but was free to diverge, which would restore the transcription defect one layer up. Identity, not equality, is what makes grading through CENSUS_BUCKETS mean anything.

mutations.name: the verdict ladder stops calling the exported bucket predicate and inlines the comparison

mutations.cell: the verdict ladder buckets rows by calling the exported predicates by name
mutations.note: The other half of the same drift: exports that the ladder no longer calls are decoration, and a test grading them would grade nothing the release path runs.
